title: Gdybyśmy, żebyśmy
title_en: The we and you-plural forms of gdyby and żeby
note:
C1 Block 7, unit 13 (path 222). FOUR NEW STRINGS - gdybysmy, gdybyscie, zebysmy, zebyscie - and ZERO new mechanism. Pays TWO logged holds at once: b2_gdyby held the plural gdyby forms as a named C1-inbox item, and b1_zeby's scope cut (inbox item 16) held the plural zeby forms. Both land here together, which is the whole argument for one unit rather than two: it is ONE person-marker family, met for the FOURTH time.

THE MARKER FAMILY IS THE UNIT, AND IT IS EXCEPTIONALLY WELL ANCHORED - every anchor verified against the position-aware pool rather than assumed. The learner has produced -smy (we) and -scie (you, more than one) in THREE separate places already: the present (jestesmy, jestescie), the past (bylismy, byliscie, robilismy, robiliscie) and the plural conditional (chcielibysmy, chcielibyscie, zrobilibyscie). So this unit adds no ending - it attaches an owned marker to two owned conjunctions. b1_zeby's own slide already told the learner the family was shared, in these words: 'The person marker is the SAME family you already own from the conditional: -m (bym), -s (bys), nothing extra for the 3rd person (by).' This unit completes that sentence.

THE ERROR THE UNIT EXISTS TO PREVENT is *Gdybysmy bylismy - the marker written twice. b2_gdyby taught the rule for the singular ('the verb straight after it is left plain: mial, byla, chcial - never a by form') and the plural is where it is easiest to break, because the plain plural L-form (byli) and the past 1pl (bylismy) differ by exactly the marker in question. Kontrola item 5 and Pisanie cloze 5 both blank that slot, with bylismy offered as a real, owned, pool-legal form in an illegal position.

THE BRIEF'S OBVIOUS HEADLINE SENTENCE IS ILLEGAL AND THIS WAS CAUGHT BY THE POOL, NOT BY EYE. 'Gdybysmy mieli czas...' is the natural first draft and it cannot be written: mieli and mialy are BOTH verified NEW. The course has never taught the plural past of miec. Every plural L-form in this pack is therefore drawn from the closed owned set byli / byly / chcieli / chcialy / kupili / kupily / zrobili / zrobily, and the if-halves run on byc and on the shop rather than on having time.

b1_conditional_pl's GRID IS DELIBERATELY PARTIAL AND THAT SHAPED EVERY RESULT CLAUSE. Verified form by form: chciec has all six plural conditionals; kupic has 1pl and 3pl but NOT 2pl (kupilibyscie is NEW); zrobic has 2pl and 3pl but NOT 1pl (zrobilibysmy is NEW). So 'we would make' is unsayable in this course and no item asks for it - the 1pl result clauses all use chcielibysmy or kupilibysmy, and the 2pl ones all use zrobilibyscie or chcielibyscie. Three drafted sentences were rewritten when this was checked. bylibysmy / byliby (the plural of the byl-conditional c1_cond_past [221] taught one node back) are also NEW and appear NOWHERE - extending that paradigm is not this unit's job, and is logged as untaught.

b1_zeby's WANTER-MUST-DIFFER-FROM-DOER RULE IS RESPECTED RATHER THAN QUIETLY BROKEN. That pack states: 'The wanter and the doer must be different people... If you want to do something yourself, you still just say chce zrobic, no zeby at all.' A first-person wanter with zebysmy (Chce, zebysmy...) puts the speaker inside the doer group and sits awkwardly against that rule. EVERY zebysmy and zebyscie item in this pack therefore uses a THIRD-PERSON wanter - Mama chce, zebysmy...; Tata chce, zebyscie... - where wanter and doer are unambiguously different and b1_zeby's rule holds exactly as written. One Kontrola item (8) keeps the owned singular zebys against a first-person wanter, which is b1_zeby's own shape.

MATCH IS THE COMPLETE MARKER PARADIGM, twelve rows: all five persons of gdyby and all five of zeby (four of them new, six owned), plus two owned plural conditionals - chcielibysmy, zrobilibyscie - so the SAME -smy/-scie markers are on the board doing their other job. That is the unit's argument made visible, and it is AGENTS' stated default recycling mechanism rather than padding.

HOMOGRAPH AND POOL DISCIPLINE. byli/byly against bylismy/byliscie is the live collision and is drilled, not dodged. dzieci takes the NON-VIRILE plural (byly, zrobilyby) and koledzy/studenci take the virile (byli, kupiliby, zrobiliby) - checked per sentence, since getting this wrong would teach a false agreement in the level that just closed the virile system. zakupy is owned and the composition zrobili zakupy follows b1_zeby's own example sentence (Chce, zebys zrobil zakupy). glodni and razem were wanted and are verified NEW, so neither appears. NO case-map.json ROW IS ADDED: this unit ships no governor.

STAGE SHAPES. Kontrola is twelve real-form choices, no meta-question, every distractor owned or taught here. Pisanie is FOUR one-word forms typed whole - the unit's entire new inventory - plus SIX cloze items, because with only four new strings the stage would otherwise have to pad or repeat; the cloze blanks fall on the load-bearing plural forms (the plain L-form after the conjunction, and the result-clause conditional), which is the queue's documented fallback and is also where the learner's error actually lives. Uzycie carries ten real sentences, all with noun subjects or objects, and every cloze frame was checked NOT to reconstruct any Uzycie sentence.

intro.title: The same two markers, for the fourth time
intro.body:
Polish marks we with -śmy and you-more-than-one with -ście, and it does it in the same way wherever the marker is needed.

You have already produced both, in three different places, without being told they were one family. Here they are.

That is the whole of this unit's new material: the two markers you see below, put onto gdyby and żeby.

intro.title: gdyby in the plural — and the verb still stays plain
intro.body:
The marker goes onto gdyby, exactly as it did in the singular.

And the rule that came with it holds: because gdyby is carrying the marker, the verb straight after it is left plain. byli, not byliśmy.

This is the one place to be careful. byli and byliśmy differ by precisely the marker gdyby has already taken, so writing it twice is the natural slip.
intro.body_pl: gdyby + śmy → gdybyśmy · gdyby + ście → gdybyście

examples.en: If we were in the shop, we would buy bread.
examples.pl: Gdybyśmy byli w sklepie, kupilibyśmy chleb.

intro.title: żeby in the plural — the same move again
intro.body:
żeby takes the two markers in the same place, and the verb after it stays plain in the same way.

Remember what this construction is for: somebody wants somebody else to do something. The one wanting and the one doing are different people, which is why the examples below have Mum or Dad doing the wanting.
intro.body_pl: żeby + śmy → żebyśmy · żeby + ście → żebyście

examples.en: Mum wants us to make dinner.
Dad wants you to buy bread.

intro.title: Both words, all five persons — the system closed
intro.body:
Nothing on this slide is a new rule. It is the two words you own, with the marker family completed.

Note that the he/she form and the they form are the same bare word — gdyby, żeby — because the marker only ever says I, you, we or you-more-than-one. It never says he or they.

match.en: that he, she or they should
that you should — more than one
you would make it — more than one

quiz.prompt: ___ byli w sklepie, kupilibyśmy chleb. (if we were in the shop)
quiz.explain: The result clause says kupilibyśmy — we — so the opener carries the same marker.

quiz.prompt: ___ byli w domu, zrobilibyście obiad. (if you — more than one — were at home)
quiz.explain: Gdybyś would be talking to one person only.

quiz.prompt: Mama chce, ___ zrobili obiad. (Mum wants us to make dinner)
quiz.explain: The doers are we, so the marker on żeby is śmy.

quiz.prompt: Tata chce, ___ kupili chleb. (Dad wants you — more than one — to buy bread)
quiz.explain: More than one doer and none of them is the speaker, so ście.

quiz.prompt: Gdybyśmy ___ w sklepie, kupilibyśmy chleb. (if we were in the shop)
quiz.explain: Gdybyśmy is already carrying the marker, so the verb stays plain. Byliśmy would mark it twice.

quiz.prompt: Chcę, żebyście ___ obiad. (I want you — more than one — to make dinner)
quiz.explain: Plain past after żeby — the marker is on żebyście and is not repeated.

quiz.prompt: Wczoraj ___ w domu. (we were at home yesterday)
quiz.explain: A plain statement about yesterday, so the marker lives on the verb — there is no gdyby to carry it.

quiz.prompt: Chcę, ___ zrobił obiad. (I want you — one man — to make dinner)
quiz.explain: One person being asked, so the singular marker ś — and zrobił is singular to match.

quiz.prompt: Gdybyśmy byli w Polsce, ___ mówić po polsku. (we would want to speak Polish)
quiz.explain: The second half keeps its own ending — this is the conditional you have owned since B1.

quiz.prompt: Gdyby studenci byli w domu, ___ obiad. (they would make dinner)
quiz.explain: Studenci are a group of men, so the virile form — and they, so by with nothing after it.

quiz.prompt: Gdybyście byli w domu, ___ obiad. (you — more than one — would make dinner)
quiz.explain: The opener said you-more-than-one, so the result clause matches it.

quiz.prompt: Mama chce, żebyśmy ___ chleb. (Mum wants us to buy bread)
quiz.explain: Plain past after żebyśmy. Kupilibyśmy belongs in a gdyby sentence, not after żeby.
